content.text: Section 2.1 expressly negates any minimum commitment, and no other clause imposes take-or-pay or volume restrictions on us.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 meets the preferred position in full: it states that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies and that Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, expressly confirming that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. Section 12.3 reinforces this by having Vendor acknowledge that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1 bars any unstated minimum-use charge. Nothing in the Order Form mechanics (§ 4.1, § 1.7) or the term and renewal provisions (§ 8.1–8.3, which allow non-renewal on thirty days' notice) creates a multi-year take-or-pay obligation. The § 22 audit "shortfall" references concern under-licensed usage true-ups, not a purchase commitment, so they do not engage this rule. No redline is warranted.
